22354-the-adventures-of-maya-the-bee.title: The Adventures Of Maya The Bee
22354-the-adventures-of-maya-the-bee.creator: Waldemar Bonsels
22354-the-adventures-of-maya-the-bee.description: A book by Waldemar Bonsels. The elderly lady-bee who helped the baby-bee Maya when she awoke to life and slipped from her cell was called Cassandra and commanded great respect in the hive. Those were exciting days. A rebellion had broken out in the nation of bees, which the queen was unable to suppress.

arxiv-2011-04330.title: Enhanced adsorption of Xe and Kr on boron doped graphene sheet decorated with transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu and Zn)
arxiv-2011-04330.creator: P. Anees
arxiv-2011-04330.description: Abstract Efficient adsorption and segregation of Xe & Kr gases is of high importance in commercial as well as nuclear industries. Systematic ab initio calculations reveal that transition-metal (TM) decorated boron-doped graphene (BDG-TM) sheet can act as an efficient substrate for adsorptive capture of Xe & Kr (adatoms).

arxiv-2012-13647.title: Generic Seebeck Effect From Spin Entropy
arxiv-2012-13647.creator: 1,2,3 Peijie Sun, 1 K. Ramesh Kumar, 1,2 Meng Lyu, 1,2 Zhen Wang, 1 Junsen Xiang, 4 Wenqing Zhang
arxiv-2012-13647.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by 1,2,3 Peijie Sun, 1 K. Ramesh Kumar, 1,2 Meng Lyu, 1,2 Zhen Wang, 1 Junsen Xiang, 4 Wenqing Zhang. How magnetism affects the Seebeck effect is an important issue widely concerned in the thermoelectric community yet remaining elusive.

arxiv-2111-08546.title: Interpreting Language Models Through Knowledge Graph Extraction
arxiv-2111-08546.creator: Vinitra Swamy, Angelika Romanou, Martin Jaggi
arxiv-2111-08546.description: Abstract Transformer-based language models trained on large text corpora have enjoyed immense popularity in the natural language processing community and are commonly used as a starting point for downstream tasks. While these models are undeniably useful, it is a challenge to quantify their performance beyond traditional accuracy metrics.

arxiv-2201-06603.title: Galois correspondence for Galois coverings on tropical curves
arxiv-2201-06603.creator: Song JuAe
arxiv-2201-06603.description: Abstract . We define Galois coverings on tropical curves for which a Galois correspondence and a universal mapping property hold. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14T15; Secondary 14T20 1. Introduction Let \varphi:\varGamma\to\varGamma^{\prime} be a map between tropical curves and G a finite group.

arxiv-2209-03020.title: Associated graded rings of the filtration of tight closure of powers of parameter ideals
arxiv-2209-03020.creator: Saipriya Dubey, Jugal Verma
arxiv-2209-03020.description: Abstract . Let I I be an ideal generated by a system of parameters in an excellent Cohen-Macaulay local domain. We show that the associated graded ring G ∗ ​ ( I ) G^{*}(I) of the filtration { ( I n ) ∗ : n ∈ ℕ } \{(I^{n})^{*}:n\in\mathbb{N}\} is Cohen-Macaulay.

arxiv-2210-10790.title: Strong Lensing by Galaxies Journal: my journal
arxiv-2210-10790.creator: A. J. Shajib 1,2,†, G. Vernardos 3,4,5,⋆, T. E. Collett 6, V. Motta 7, D. Sluse 8, L. L. R. Williams 9, P. Saha 10, S. Birrer 11,12,13, C. Spiniello 14,15, T. Treu 16
arxiv-2210-10790.description: Abstract Strong gravitational lensing at the galaxy scale is a valuable tool for various applications in astrophysics and cosmology. Some of the primary uses of galaxy-scale lensing are to study elliptical galaxies’ mass structure and evolution, constrain the stellar initial mass function, and measure cosmological parameters.

arxiv-2211-01317.title: Low-Resource Music Genre Classification with Cross-Modal Neural Model Reprogramming
arxiv-2211-01317.creator: Yun-Ning Hung, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Pin-Yu Chen, Alexander Lerch
arxiv-2211-01317.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yun-Ning Hung, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Pin-Yu Chen, Alexander Lerch. Transfer learning (TL) approaches have shown promising results when handling tasks with limited training data. However, considerable memory and computational resources are often required for fine-tuning pre-trained neural networks with target domain data . In this work, we introduce a novel method for leveraging pre-trained speech models for low-resource music classification based on the concept of Neural Model Reprogramming (NMR) .

arxiv-2309-13334.title: Neighborly partitions, Hypergraphs and Gordon’s identities
arxiv-2309-13334.creator: Pooneh Afsharijoo and Hussein Mourtada
arxiv-2309-13334.description: Abstract . We prove a family of partition identities which is "dual" to the family of Andrews-Gordon’s identities. These identities are inspired by a correspondence between a special type of partitions and "hypergraphs" and their proof uses combinatorial commutative algebra. † † keywords: Andrew-Gordon’s identities; integer partitions; graded algebras; Hypergraphs; Hilbert series.

arxiv-2404-03377.title: Alternating Quantifiers in Uniform One-Dimensional Fragments with an Excursion into Three-Variable Logic
arxiv-2404-03377.creator: Oskar Fiuk ORCID:0009-0006-1312-4899, Emanuel Kieroński ORCID:0000-0002-8538-8221
arxiv-2404-03377.description: Abstract . The uniform one-dimensional fragment of first-order logic was introduced a few years ago as a generalization of the two-variable fragment to contexts involving relations of arity greater than two. Quantifiers in this logic are used in blocks, each block consisting only of existential quantifiers or only of universal quantifiers.

arxiv-2405-18570.title: It’s Not a Modality Gap: Characterizing and Addressing the Contrastive Gap
arxiv-2405-18570.creator: Abrar Fahim, Alex Murphy, Alona Fyshe
arxiv-2405-18570.description: Abstract Multi-modal contrastive models such as CLIP ( Radford et al. 2021 ) achieve state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot classification by embedding input images and texts on a joint representational space. Recently, a modality gap has been reported in two-encoder contrastive models like CLIP, meaning that the image and text embeddings reside in disjoint areas of the latent space.

arxiv-2409-12396.title: ARTAI: An Evaluation Platform to Assess Societal Risk of Recommender Algorithms Conference: FAccTRec 2024: The 7th Workshop on Responsible Recommendation. In 18th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems; October 14–18, 2024; Bari, Italy
arxiv-2409-12396.creator: Qin Ruan, Jin Xu, Ruihai Dong, Arjumand Younus, Tai Tan Mai, Barry O’Sullivan, Susan Leavy
arxiv-2409-12396.description: Abstract . Societal risk emanating from how recommender algorithms disseminate content online is now well documented. Emergent regulation aims to mitigate this risk through ethical audits and enabling new research on the social impact of algorithms. However, there is currently a need for tools and methods that enable such evaluation.

arxiv-2505-02697.title: Uniformization of metric surfaces: A survey
arxiv-2505-02697.creator: Dimitrios Ntalampekos
arxiv-2505-02697.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios Ntalampekos. In this survey we present the most recent developments in the uniformization of metric surfaces, i.e., metric spaces homeomorphic to two-dimensional topological manifolds. We start from the classical conformal uniformization theorem of Koebe and Poincaré. Then we discuss the Bonk–Kleiner theorem on the quasisymmetric uniformization of metric spheres, which marks the beginning of the study of the uniformization problem on fractal surfaces. The next result presented is Rajala’s theorem on the quasiconformal uniformization of metric spheres.

pmc-10514712.title: Relationships among body weight, lipids and bone mass in elderly individuals with fractures: A case-control study
pmc-10514712.creator: Xiang-Xu Chen, Chu-Wei Tian, Li-Yong Bai, Ya-Kuan Zhao, Cheng Zhang, Liu Shi, Yuan-Wei Zhang, Wen-Jun Xie, Huan-Yi Zhu, Hui Chen, Yun-Feng Rui
pmc-10514712.description: BACKGROUNDThe prevalence of osteoporosis and low bone mass is steadily rising each year. Low body weight is commonly linked to diminished bone mass and serves as a robust predictor of osteoporosis. Nonetheless, the connection between body mass index (BMI), bone mineral density, and lipid profiles among the elderly remains elusive.

pmc-11393080.title: Tipping-point transition from transient to persistent inflammation in pancreatic islets
pmc-11393080.creator: Thomas Holst-Hansen, Pernille Yde Nielsen, Mogens H. Jensen, Thomas Mandrup-Poulsen, Ala Trusina
pmc-11393080.description: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with a systemic increase in the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1β. While transient exposure to low IL-1β concentrations improves insulin secretion and β-cell proliferation in pancreatic islets, prolonged exposure leads to impaired insulin secretion and collective β-cell death.

pmc-11626061.title: The concepts of Intra Spinal Pressure (ISP), Intra Thecal Pressure (ITP), and Spinal Cord Perfusion Pressure (SCPP) in acute, severe traumatic spinal cord injury: Narrative review
pmc-11626061.creator: Samira Saadoun, Hasan Asif, Marios C. Papadopoulos
pmc-11626061.description: There is increasing interest in monitoring pressure from the injured spinal cord to guide the management of patients with acute, severe traumatic spinal cord injuries (TSCI). This is analogous to monitoring intracranial pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure in traumatic brain injury (TBI). Here, we explore key concepts in this field and novel therapies that are emerging from these ideas.

pmc-12551151.title: Supervising physicians’ perceptions on physician work-hour regulations in Japan: a nationwide cross-sectional study
pmc-12551151.creator: Hirohisa Fujikawa, Hidetaka Tamune, Yuji Nishizaki, Kiyoshi Shikino, Taro Shimizu, Yu Yamamoto, Miwa Sekine, Kazuya Nagasaki, Hiroyuki Kobayashi, Yasuharu Tokuda
pmc-12551151.description: PurposeJapan introduced physician work-hour regulations in April 2024. Perceptions of such regulations appear to be influenced by history and culture, and thus vary among stakeholders and countries. Here, we aimed to investigate supervising physicians’ perceptions of physician work-hour regulations in Japan.MethodsA nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted from March to April, 2024.

pmc-13118034.title: EHMN 2026: A Thermodynamically Refined, SBML-Standardised Human Metabolic Network for Genome-Scale Analysis and QSP Integration
pmc-13118034.creator: Igor Goryanin, Leonid Slovianov, Stephen Checkley, Irina Goryanin
pmc-13118034.description: Background: Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are foundational tools for systems biology, enabling quantitative interrogation of human metabolism across physiological and pathological states. However, many legacy reconstructions exhibit heterogeneous identifier usage, incomplete pathway integration, and limited thermodynamic refinement, constraining reproducibility, interoperability, and translational applicability. Methods: We present EHMN 2026, an update of the Edinburgh Human Metabolic Network.

pmc-13406683.title: Megakaryocyte–Platelet Immunometabolism in Leukemic Niche Remodeling
pmc-13406683.creator: Hoyeop Baek, Kiwon Lee
pmc-13406683.description: Simple SummaryMegakaryocytes are increasingly recognized as active regulators of bone marrow remodeling in hematopoietic malignancies, extending their role far beyond platelet production. Recent studies show that abnormal megakaryocytes and platelets release inflammatory molecules and small extracellular particles that alter immune responses, blood vessel function, and communication between cells within the bone marrow.

pmc-13409325.creator: Daniel Chan, Harshini Katugampola, Mehul T Dattani

pmc-13438318.title: A machine learning-based risk prediction model for early preterm birth: development and prospective validation
pmc-13438318.creator: Liang He, Kailin Luo, Rong Wang, Gaoying Wang, Jianyi Gao, Jing Wang, Ruirui Dong
pmc-13438318.description: IntroductionPreterm birth (PTB) remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet accurate and clinically applicable risk prediction tools during mid-pregnancy are still limited.MethodsWe developed a machine learning–based model to predict PTB risk using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data obtained during mid-pregnancy.

pmc-13439410.title: Voriconazole pseudotoxicity: a case report highlighting the importance of sampling timing in TDM interpretation by clinical pharmacists
pmc-13439410.creator: Xiao-Ming Deng, Yuan Xu, Zhi-Qi Xie, Jun-Jie Xu, Kai-Li Mao, Hua-Yu Sun
pmc-13439410.description: This case report describes a 57-year-old male patient who sought medical attention due to severe pneumonia and respiratory failure. The initial empirical antibiotic treatment was ineffective. Bronchoscopy and lung alveolar lavage fluid culture confirmed a case of Aspergillus fumigatus infection.

pmc-13470336.title: Comparative efficacy of exercise modes on inflammatory cytokines in patients with breast cancer: a systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analyses
pmc-13470336.creator: Mousa Khalafi, Mohammad Hossein Sakhaei, Faeghe Ghasemi, Saeid Fatolahi, Kosar Omidian, Michael E Symonds, Hadi Rohani, Sara K Rosenkranz, Katsuhiko Suzuki, Ayda Sadat Zakeri, Marziyeh Mohammadiyan, Shima Mojtahedi, Aref Habibi Maleki, Hossein Rafiei
pmc-13470336.description: Cytokines play a key role in the pathogenesis and progression of breast cancer and are increasingly recognized as potential therapeutic targets. The anti-inflammatory effects of regular exercise training are well-established, but its effects on inflammatory adipocytokines in individuals with breast cancer have not been elucidated.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Findings The Congress finds and declares that— (1) education is important to, and makes a significant contribution to, the readjustment of incarcerated individuals to society; and (2) there is a growing need for immediate action by the Federal Government.
